judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass Senate Bill 2. It created education savings accounts that families can use for private school tuition and other approved education costs. Each account gets 85 percent of average state and local funding per public school student, and the first two-year program budget is capped at $1 billion. The bill became law after the Texas Senate passed it 19-12.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to send House Joint Resolution 2 to Texas voters. It would block new or higher state taxes on estates, inheritances, or gifts beyond those in place on January 1, 2025. The Texas House approved it 112-29 and put it on the November 4, 2025 statewide ballot.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to send House Joint Resolution 4 to Texas voters. It would block taxes on securities trades and on the business of running a registered securities market. General business, sales, and use taxes could continue. The Texas House approved it 111-31 and put it on the November 4, 2025 statewide ballot.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to send House Joint Resolution 34 to Texas voters. It would let lawmakers exempt the added value from border security structures on land in counties next to Mexico from property tax. The Texas Senate approved it 23-8 and put it on the November 4, 2025 statewide ballot.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to send Senate Joint Resolution 18 to Texas voters. It would permanently bar state taxes on capital gains, which are profits from selling assets, for individuals, families, estates, and trusts. Texas had no such tax, so this would block a future one while leaving property, sales, and use taxes in place. The Texas Senate approved it 24-6 and put it on the November 4, 2025 statewide ballot.

judgments.yea_description: Voted through House Joint Resolution 98 to ask Congress for a constitutional convention, a national meeting that can suggest changes to the United States Constitution. Any change had to limit federal spending or power, or set term limits for federal officers and members of Congress. The Texas House backed the request 86-57 and the Senate 17-14. It was filed with the Secretary of State on May 13, 2025, making Texas's application to Congress official. Applications to Congress do not go to Texas voters.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass Senate Bill 8. It requires every county sheriff who runs a jail to seek a deal that lets local officers help enforce federal immigration law. State grants cover the cost, and the attorney general can sue a sheriff who does not comply. The bill became law after the Texas House passed it 86-47.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass Senate Bill 2972. It limits a public college free-speech law to students and employees, and common outdoor campus areas no longer get the law's strongest protection for public speech. Schools must bar camping, speech events from 10 at night to 8 in the morning, and masks used to evade rules, scare people, or block campus officials. The bill became law after the Texas House passed it 97-39.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass Senate Bill 12. It bars public schools from assigning diversity, equity, and inclusion duties or teaching about sexual orientation or gender identity in any grade. Schools cannot sponsor clubs based on those topics, and parents must give written permission for clubs and human sexuality lessons. The bill became law after the Texas House passed it 88-47.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to accept the final House-Senate deal on Senate Bill 13. It gives elected school boards final approval of library books after at least 30 days of public review. Parents may block their child from certain books, and a challenged book stays unavailable to students until the district decides. The bill became law after the Texas House approved it 81-48.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass Senate Bill 15. In cities over 150,000 people in larger counties, it caps lot-size rules on land of at least five acres not yet divided into lots. Cities cannot demand lots over 3,000 square feet, 30 feet wide, or 75 feet deep; affected people may sue to enforce these limits. The bill became law after the Texas House passed it 86-43.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to accept the final House-Senate deal on Senate Bill 17. It bars governments, companies, and some people tied to countries named as security threats from buying Texas property. United States citizens and green-card holders are exempt; a covered person who buys on purpose can face the lowest felony level and a forced sale. The bill became law after the Texas House approved it 85-57.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to accept the final House-Senate deal on Senate Bill 37. Public college boards must review basic required courses every five years and may reverse course changes or some senior hires. Only boards may create faculty senates, which can only give advice; a governor-chosen official handles college complaints. The bill became law after the Texas House approved it 83-47.
